hook: Who is speaking, the source or the author? Read a feuilleton on slowness and let the verb forms tell you.
intro: A feuilleton article of about 410 words on the rediscovery of slowness. It has a clear architecture: an elevated opening with a triple sei es … sei es … sei es; two experts who disagree, both reported in the Konjunktiv I (the sociologist Karin Wendt: Die neue Langsamkeit sei daher weniger Nostalgie als Notwehr.; the economist Thomas Berger: Langsamkeit, so Berger, lasse sich nur deshalb so gut verkaufen, weil sie knapp geworden sei.); then the author’s own verdict in the indicative (Beide haben recht, und gerade darin liegt das Interessante.), an ironic aside (gemächlich, versteht sich) and a closing warning. The questions ask what each source claims, how the author weighs them, and what the ending means – so first sort every sentence by voice: Konjunktiv = a source, indicative = the author.
tips[0].title: Source or author? Look at the verb form
tips[0].text: The press reports a source’s claims in the Konjunktiv I, and only forms that differ from the indicative can mark this: sei, habe, könne, werde, lasse, bringe, erzeuge, verliere. Where the Konjunktiv I is identical to the indicative – as in the plural haben – the Konjunktiv II hätten stands in. Everything in the plain indicative is the author speaking. A weak-verb form such as entdeckten would not help: it looks exactly like the Präteritum, which is why the article writes hätten … neu entdeckt.
tips[0].trap: The framing verbs are indicative (Er hält die Bewegung für …, widerspricht): they report that someone speaks; what they say follows in the Konjunktiv.
tips[0].check.why: seien is Konjunktiv I and belongs to the economist; hat reagiert is plain indicative, so that sentence is the author speaking.
tips[0].visual.rows[0].a: Langsamkeit sei ein Luxus, heißt es.
tips[0].visual.rows[0].b: Vielleicht könnte sie aber eine Notwendigkeit sein.
tips[1].title: The author hedges with könnte
tips[1].text: The one Konjunktiv II in the author’s voice is a hedge, not a report: könnte sich als … erweisen presents a cautious judgement. Read it together with the indicative sentence that follows it, which adds the reservation.
tips[1].trap: „Marotte“ is only how it seems at first (zunächst … anmutet), not the author’s verdict.
tips[1].check.why: A Konjunktiv II in the author’s voice is a hedge: a careful verdict, not a report of someone else’s words.
tips[2].title: The feuilleton’s devices
tips[2].text: zum Maß aller Dinge erheben (to elevate to the measure of all things – an echo of Protagoras), the triple sei es … sei es … sei es (be it …, be it …), the ironic aside, and a closing sentence that turns the topic against itself. Questions on the ending are answered from the last sentence alone.
tips[2].trap: sei es … sei es is a fixed formula for listing examples; it does not mark reported speech.
tips[2].check.why: sei es … sei es is a fixed formula for listing alternatives; it does not signal that someone else is being quoted.
remember[0]: Konjunktiv I (sei, habe, könne, werde, lasse) or hätten = a source; indicative = the author.
remember[1]: A weak-verb Konjunktiv II like entdeckten looks like the Präteritum and marks nothing.
remember[2]: könnte sich als … erweisen = the author’s hedge; the last sentence = the warning.
remember[3]: sei es … sei es; zum Maß aller Dinge erheben; weniger A als B.
exam: Long opinion pieces with several reported sources are a C2 exam reading text — and the feuilleton of every serious German weekend paper.
tips[0].check.q: „Die Mieten, so der Ökonom, seien stark gestiegen. Die Stadt hat inzwischen reagiert.“ Who states that the city has reacted?
tips[1].check.q: In the author’s own voice: „Das Projekt könnte sich als Fehlschlag erweisen.“ What does könnte do?
tips[1].check.options[0]: It gives the author’s cautious judgement
tips[1].check.options[1]: It reports what a source said
tips[1].check.answer: It gives the author’s cautious judgement
tips[2].check.q: „Viele suchen die Stille, sei es im Kloster, sei es im Wald.“ What does sei es … sei es do here?
tips[2].check.options[0]: It lists examples: be it … or …
tips[2].check.answer: It lists examples: be it … or …
